tasks.task: Reply to a batch of reviews

items.when: Each week, or daily for busy venues and apps, to run the reply desk in a fixed order
When reviews from several platforms need sorting into buckets and a reply for each
When you have one batch to answer now, with risky ones held for the owner
Before replying, to rank the batch by tone, urgency and warning signs
When replies start to sound the same, to get a second set written a different way
When reviews arrive in a steady stream and each batch needs checked replies
Before a reply to an upset reviewer is posted, to check promises, facts and tone

tasks.task: Write a careful reply to one bad review

items.when: When one negative review has upset the owner and needs a public reply and a private note
When you want a second draft that names the feeling first, to compare with yours
When the reviewer was a hotel or restaurant guest and the reply needs a fair fix
Before the owner approves, to check each promise in the reply can be kept
When the reply says sorry but then explains it away, to apologise without a 'but'
When the private message must calm someone who feels unheard

tasks.task: Write a review reply guide for the team

items.when: When several people reply to reviews and the business sounds like different firms
When there is no written voice yet, to set tone by situation with word lists
When the team needs one page with before and after examples, to compare formats
When the guide is in use, to check real replies against it and rank the slips

tasks.task: Report the month's repeat complaints and praise

items.when: When a month of reviews from every platform needs ranking with counts, quotes and trend
When you paste product reviews and need complaints, praise and requests ranked
When you need the reason behind each review named before you count them
When low reviews may come from people the product was never for
Each month, to keep one running record of what customers say across sources
When the same complaint returns every month, to trace it to the step that causes it

tasks.task: Run the monthly reputation review with the owner

items.when: In the first week of each month, for about an hour of work and 20 minutes with the owner
Before the review, to gather ratings and mentions from many sites in one report
When talk about the business happens outside review sites, to group it by theme
When the owner wants ratings, volume and reply times written up with what to change

tasks.task: Plan how to earn more reviews the honest way

items.when: When you write the ask: the same for every customer, no rewards and no filtering
When replies and a plan to get more reviews are needed in one run
When you must decide the moment to ask and the channel to ask through
When a shop needs the list of buyers whose order arrived a week or two ago
When review emails go unopened, to compare subject lines from several angles
Before the ask is sent, to check it pressures nobody and steers no one to five stars

tasks.task: Decide whether to flag a review and file the flag

items.when: When one review may break a platform's rules and you must decide and write the flag
When you need the rule it breaks, the evidence and the platform's own tool to file through
When reviews look planted, to get a trust rating and the red flags behind it
Before flagging, to split the review's false facts from opinion, which platforms keep

tasks.task: Respond to a burst of bad reviews or a viral complaint

items.when: When one and two-star reviews arrive in a burst, look coordinated or come with a demand
When many of the reviews break platform rules and need flags with evidence
When the cause is a real failure and you need who to tell and what to do for 30 days
When you must judge whether the burst is real customers or a campaign
When the complaint is spreading on social media and you need what is being said
When the first instinct is to defend the firm, to start from the people affected

tasks.task: Write private replies that put a complaint right

items.when: When a reviewer is contacted privately and the reply must fit their situation
When the business was at fault and owes a short apology that says what happens next
When the reviewer wants money back and the answer is yes, partial or no
Before sending, to check the facts, the promises and the tone
When the reply follows policy but leaves the customer no better off
When you ask one happy customer, with three questions and a note on how words are used
When you plan who to ask, when, and how each answer is approved and recorded
When the first request gets thin answers, to try a different set of questions
When a shop needs its best customers listed so you know who to ask first
When a customer said yes but has not replied, to nudge with a new reason
Before the request is sent, to cut it down and check it asks for one thing

tasks.task: Build a testimonial library with permissions tracked

items.when: When quotes sit in inboxes and nobody knows which may be used or where
Each month, to add new reviews, check approved quotes and link claims to evidence
When a quote states a result, to check the business holds evidence for it
Before filming, to record what the customer agrees to and where the video will run
When you need questions that draw out the before, the choice and the result on camera
When written reviews should become a video script with every line sourced
When a customer's recording needs trimming and captions by editing the transcript

tasks.task: Set up a customer advocate programme

items.when: When a shop wants its best customers known, thanked and invited to speak up
When you have a budget for the top customers and want a plan with a control group
When advocates might also refer friends and you want a reward design to consider
When you want customers posting their own photos and stories about the business
When the programme touches reviews, to check no reward is tied to leaving one

tasks.task: Turn the best reviews into proof for pages and ads

items.when: When you know buyers' doubts and must pick which quote answers each and where
When review lines should become quote cards, to plan several with pictures and text
When reviews should drive an ad, to get an angle and copy built from buyers' words
When ratings should show in search results and the page needs working markup
Before a quote is published, to confirm consent covers this use and the edit is fair

tasks.task: Turn a happy customer into a case story

items.when: When one customer interview should become a case outline with the evidence gaps listed
Before the call, to plan questions that follow the customer's own timeline
When the customer has no time for a call and will answer three written questions

tasks.task: Track what people say about the business beyond reviews

items.when: When you need reviews, ratings and mentions from many sites in one report
When you need social talk about the brand grouped by theme with notable posts
When comments under the brand's own posts hold questions and complaints to sort
When forum threads about the category keep being cited and you must pick which to answer

tasks.task: Check what search and AI tools say about the business

items.when: When an AI tool states wrong facts about the business, to list each with its fix
When the owner asks where the brand is mentioned online and how strongly
When the map listing shows wrong hours, categories or photos next to the reviews
When a shop wants its star ratings and store badge to show on Google

tasks.task: Analyse survey, NPS and feedback comments

items.when: When you have NPS, CSAT or open comments and need themes and trends in a report
When feedback comes from tickets, surveys and calls and needs one ranked signal
When there is no survey yet and you need short questions to send after purchase
Before acting on a survey, to see which answers can be trusted

tasks.task: Trace a repeat complaint to its cause and hand over a fix

items.when: When you must name the one fix that would remove the most complaints
When a problem keeps coming back and needs a checked chain of whys
When related tickets and reviews should be read together for a shared cause
When people keep getting the same thing wrong and the design may be at fault
When the cause may be the promise on the page, not the product or service

always.when: At the start with a new client, to set the voice every reply and request follows
When a reply or proof line states a fact about the business you cannot trace
Before replies are posted in public, to catch typos and names spelt two ways

helpers.when: When a review needs the order looked up, a refund made or a case worked to the end
When a complaint reaches the press or needs a public statement
When repeat complaints point to a broken journey that needs redesigning
When the map listing and local pages need fixing alongside the reviews
When a review ask, reward or takedown may break consumer law or sector rules
When video testimonials need filming, editing and versions for each channel

gaps: No library item knows each platform's review rules for Google, Trustpilot, Yelp, Tripadvisor or app stores; only the kit does
No library item builds an evidence pack for a review flag or drafts the next step when a platform refuses
No library item handles a coordinated review attack or a demand for money to remove reviews
No library item records testimonial consent: what was agreed, where it may be used and when it lapses
No library item makes a video testimonial kit: questions, a filming guide for a phone and a release form
No library item sets up a B2B reference customer programme with reference calls and no reward for reviews
No library item explains consumer law on review incentives, gating and fake reviews by country
No library item works on the search results for a brand name or a knowledge panel
No library item covers employer review sites or marketplace seller feedback
No library item scores a team's past review replies against its reply guide
No library item writes the private follow-up message that goes with a public review reply
